title: Compact progress lane notes - personal KPI pulse
content:
Compact Progress Lane — Weeks 1–3

Purpose: quick, low-friction record of what I actually shipped vs what I planned. Keep it short so I actually update it during the week. Not a formal retro — more of a running scratchpad to catch patterns.

Baseline metrics (for this 3-week cadence):
- Deep focus hours per week (target): 18h (actual week1 15h, week2 19h, week3 17h)
- PRs merged (personal): target 3/wk -> week1 2, week2 4, week3 3
- Experiments started: target 2/week -> week1 1, week2 2, week3 2
- User-facing bug count reduced (my area): baseline 7 -> now 4
- Mood / energy (1–5): W1 3, W2 4, W3 3

Quick notes (freeform):
- Week1: got distracted by debugging infra flakiness; lost two deep blocks. Need to reserve 2h On-Call buffer in calendar next cycle.
- Week2: shipped the small batching heuristic; saw a small reduction in token latency in dev load tests (~6%). Patch PR linked above. Felt very productive.
- Week3: switched to shorter, earlier deep work blocks (8:30–10:30) — helped, but afternoon meetings still fragment.

Hypotheses to test next cadence:
1) If I schedule a 90-min focus block right after stand-up (9:30–11:00), then weekly deep hours will increase by ~2–3h.
2) If I batch smaller PRs and label them "quick-ships", I can increase merge throughput without increasing review time.
3) If I capture 1 blocker in a short daily note at EOD, then unblocked rate will rise.

Measurement plan:
- Add a calendar tag "deep:kyra" and count occurrences; cross-check against manual tally.
- Track PRs labeled quick-ship using GitHub search query and weekly export.
- Add a single-line daily note in this doc each evening: time, top blocker, 1 thing done.

Mini action list (next 2 weeks):
- Add 2x 90-min deep blocks to calendar for next Monday/Wednesday (ACTION by 2025-02-05).
- Create GitHub label "quick-ship-kyra" and add to small PRs (ACTION: create label -> link PRs).
- On-call buffer: reserve Tue 15:00–17:00 as buffer for infra follow-ups.
- Write short guidance doc for reviewer checklist (3 bullets) and link on PRs.

Risks & friction:
- Calendar fragmentation from recurring syncs — consider moving one weekly sync to async update.
- Reviewer latency — if reviewers >48h we lose momentum. Possible mitigations: add reviewer on-call rotation for small PRs.

Mini-retro (what worked / what didn't):
- Worked: shorter morning deep blocks; quick-ship label increased PR throughput when reviewers were available.
- Didn't work: trying to do long afternoons; energy drops.

Questions / unresolved:
- Is it worth blocking reviewer time 1x/week or just nudging reviewers? (need to try both)
- What is the minimum experiment size that reliably yields valuable signal? (I think ~30m–2h dev effort)

Daily EOD template (to copy into note):
- Date | deep hours today | top blocker | one concrete thing shipped | energy 1–5

Sample EOD entries (week3):
- 2025-01-27 | 2h | waiting on infra rollout | merged batching tweak | 3
- 2025-01-28 | 1.5h | flaky CI job | wrote reviewer checklist draft | 3

Reference links / context:
- Linear ticket for batching heuristic: https://linear.app/RI/issue/ENG-621
- Playground PR with experiment code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playground/pull/88
- Quick reviewer checklist draft (TODO add to repo): 1) small PR summary line, 2) test pointers, 3) rollback note.

End note: keep this doc lightweight. If the daily EOD becomes >3 lines, migrate to a structured sheet. Next sync with Maya to align reviewer experiment on 2025-02-03.
